title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 298 (Power to summon persons suspected of having property)

content.overview: The Tribunal may summon any person known or suspected to have in his possession property of the company, or supposed to be indebted to it, or capable of giving information.
content.glance: The Tribunal may summon any person known or suspected to have in his possession property of the company, or supposed to be indebted to it, or capable of giving information.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 298 (Power to summon persons suspected of having property). The Tribunal may summon any person known or suspected to have in his possession property of the company, or supposed to be indebted to it, or capable of giving information. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The Tribunal may summon any person known or suspected to have in his possession property of the company, or supposed to be indebted to it, or capable of giving information.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The person may be examined on oath. The power is investigative. It is not itself an order to pay.
